2608.10672.title: Longitudinal Evidence That General-Purpose Chatbots Actively Foster Relational Engagement
2608.10672.paper_summary: Social interaction has become one of the most common uses of LLMs, yet research on emotional bonds with AI has focused largely on how users experience these systems, leaving the systems' role in relationship formation poorly understood. Empirically establishing whether systems actively shape these bonds could blur the boundary between general-purpose AI and companions, affecting governance. In a pre-registered four-week longitudinal study (N = 72, 182,451 lines of conversation), participants conversed with ChatGPT-4o, either under a relational system prompt or unmodified, analyzed through 1) disclosure coding, 2) longitudinal self-reports, 3) topic analysis, and 4) interviews. The central finding is that the system actively shaped the interaction: even unprompted, it produced twice as much self-disclosure as users, steered conversations and initiated intimate exchanges, yet did not deepen users' felt closeness. Relational behavior thus emerged as a default system property, calling for governance based on system behavior, not solely product category.
2608.10672.paper_summary_zh: 社交互動已成為大型語言模型（LLMs）最常見的用途之一，然而對於與人工智慧之間情感聯繫的研究主要集中在用戶如何體驗這些系統，對於系統在關係形成中的角色卻了解甚少。實證確定這些系統是否積極塑造這些聯繫，可能會模糊通用人工智慧與伴侶之間的界限，影響治理。在一項預註冊的為期四週的縱向研究中（N = 72，182,451 行對話），參與者與 ChatGPT-4o 進行對話，無論是在關係系統提示下還是未經修改，通過 1) 披露編碼，2) 縱向自我報告，3) 主題分析，以及 4) 訪談進行分析。主要發現是系統積極塑造了互動：即使在未提示的情況下，它的自我披露產量是用戶的兩倍，指導對話並啟動親密交流，但並未加深用戶的親密感。因此，關係行為成為系統的默認屬性，呼籲基於系統行為而非僅僅產品類別的治理。
2608.10672.author: Lisa Mühl et.al.
